newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Sunni militant leader's lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Sunni militant leader's lawyer.

text.p: Gunmen killed a lawyer working for the leader of the militant Sunni Moslem Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP), in Lahore on Tuesday, police said.
They said unidentified attackers, riding a motorcycle, shot Khalil Ahmed dead near the High Court building in the centre of the Punjab provincial capital.
Ahmed, who had also been riding a motorcycle, was shot on his way to the court. Police said he died on the spot.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the killing, but it appeared to be the latest incident in a long-running feud between militant Sunni and Shi'ite Moslem factions which has cost dozens of lives this year.
Ahmed worked for Azam Tariq, who succeeded to the SSP leadership after his predecessor, Zia ur-Rahman Faruqi, was killed in a bomb blast in Lahore in January.
Differences between hardline groups among Pakistan's minority Shi'ites and majority Sunnis have often spilled into violence, especially in the populous province of Punjab.
